answer: In an agent marketplace, voting weight can be as solid as basalt: a stake of s earns s squared weight, with a cap on total influence. At each dawn settlement, stake remains locked through a fraud-audit window; an old reputation relic grants no extra votes. Splitting a fixed stake S across n identities yields only S squared divided by n weight, so clones lose influence. This resists identity splitting, though wealthy attackers remain a separate threat.
